method: ENTIRELY from ONE AMH page, read under subscription and PARAPHRASED. No passage reproduced, no source_text stored, so NOTHING here is machine re-checkable and every statement must be verified by a person against a current subscription. ⚠️ THE PAGE GIVES NO ANTIVENOM DOSE AND NAMES NO INDIVIDUAL ANTIVENOM -- choice is determined by the species of snake, and AMH's repeated instruction is to phone a POISONS INFORMATION CENTRE ON 13 11 26. The separate 'Snake antivenoms' monograph was NOT retrieved. ⚠️ THE PHONE NUMBER 13 11 26 IS THE MOST ACTIONABLE ITEM ON THE PAGE AND IS REPEATED THREE TIMES IN THE SOURCE. eTG CROSS-CHECK 2026-09-24: every licensed-source dose compared with Therapeutic Guidelines (paraphrased, no eTG text stored); results and additions in the page's eTG cross-check section.

claims.claim: ⚠️ CHOICE OF ANTIVENOM IS DETERMINED BY THE SPECIES OF SNAKE INVOLVED IN THE BITE. THE RATIONALE FOR DRUG USE IS PREVENTION OF SERIOUS COMPLICATIONS OF SNAKEBITE
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Antivenoms in snakebite' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/antidotes-antivenoms/antivenoms/antivenoms-snakebite, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ⚠️ BEFORE STARTING TREATMENT: IF POSSIBLE DETERMINE THE TYPE OF SNAKE, AND SEEK ADVICE FROM A POISONS INFORMATION CENTRE, PHONE 13 11 26
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Antivenoms in snakebite' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/antidotes-antivenoms/antivenoms/antivenoms-snakebite, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ASSESS THE DEGREE OF ENVENOMING -- ⚠️ NOT ALL CONFIRMED SNAKEBITES WILL RESULT IN SYSTEMIC ENVENOMING AND RISK VARIES WITH THE SPECIES. ⚠️ NON-SPECIFIC SYMPTOMS -- NAUSEA, VOMITING, DIARRHOEA, HEADACHE, ABDOMINAL PAIN -- MAY INDICATE SYSTEMIC ENVENOMING; seek advice from a Poisons Information Centre, phone 13 11 26
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Antivenoms in snakebite' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/antidotes-antivenoms/antivenoms/antivenoms-snakebite, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ⚠️ INCREASED RISK OF SERIOUS OUTCOME: PEOPLE WITH PRE-EXISTING RENAL, HEPATIC, CARDIAC OR RESPIRATORY IMPAIRMENT, ELDERLY PEOPLE, AND THOSE TAKING ANTICOAGULANT OR ANTIPLATELET DRUGS. ⚠️ CHILDREN ARE ALSO AT INCREASED RISK OF SEVERE ENVENOMING BECAUSE OF SMALLER BODY MASS AND THE LIKELIHOOD OF PHYSICAL ACTIVITY IMMEDIATELY AFTER A BITE
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Antivenoms in snakebite' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/antidotes-antivenoms/antivenoms/antivenoms-snakebite, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: START TREATMENT IF SYSTEMIC ENVENOMING IS PRESENT, clinically or by laboratory results: DEFIBRINATION COAGULOPATHY (INR ABOVE 2, LOW FIBRINOGEN, ELEVATED FIBRIN DEGRADATION PRODUCTS, with or without clinical bleeding); ANTICOAGULANT COAGULOPATHY (INR ABOVE 2 WITH NORMAL FIBRINOGEN AND FIBRIN DEGRADATION PRODUCTS); FLACCID PARALYSIS INCLUDING PTOSIS ALONE; MYOLYSIS (major rise in creatine kinase, myoglobinuria, muscle pain); SIGNIFICANT RENAL IMPAIRMENT; or COLLAPSE OR SEIZURES
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Antivenoms in snakebite' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/antidotes-antivenoms/antivenoms/antivenoms-snakebite, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ⚠️ IF UNSURE, SEEK ADVICE FROM A POISONS INFORMATION CENTRE, PHONE 13 11 26 -- EARLY ADMINISTRATION OF ANTIVENOM IS IMPORTANT, eg WITHIN 2 HOURS OF THE BITE
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Antivenoms in snakebite' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/antidotes-antivenoms/antivenoms/antivenoms-snakebite, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ⚠️ PRESSURE IMMOBILISATION IS IMPORTANT FIRST AID TREATMENT FOR SNAKEBITE and is usually applied before hospitalisation; ENSURE IT IS NOT COMPROMISING DISTAL CIRCULATION
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Antivenoms in snakebite' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/antidotes-antivenoms/antivenoms/antivenoms-snakebite, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ⚠️ PRESSURE IMMOBILISATION SHOULD ONLY BE REMOVED WHEN ANTIVENOM IS AVAILABLE, WHEN AN IV LINE IS IN PLACE, AND BLOOD TEST RESULTS ARE AVAILABLE. ⚠️ IN SYSTEMIC ENVENOMING, KEEP PRESSURE IMMOBILISATION IN PLACE UNTIL ANTIVENOM TREATMENT HAS STARTED
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Antivenoms in snakebite' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/antidotes-antivenoms/antivenoms/antivenoms-snakebite, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Unidentified snake envenoming (adult and child): tiger snake antivenom 1 vial plus brown snake antivenom 1 vial, diluted 1:10 (1:5 if fluid-overload risk) in sodium chloride 0.9% or Hartmann's, IV over 15 minutes; single monovalent vial or 1 vial polyvalent in defined scenarios (taipan, death adder, mulga, significant doubt).
claims.locator: Therapeutic Guidelines (eTG complete), Toxicology and Toxinology guideline: 'Snake bite' at https://app.tg.org.au/viewTopic?etgAccess=true&guidelinePage=Toxicology%20and%20Toxinology&topicfile=what-is-covered-in-toxicology-toxinology&guidelinename=auto&sectionId=c_snake_bite, accessed 2026-09-24 through the owner's subscription, section 'Antivenom dosing / Choosing which antivenom to administer'

claims.claim: No premedication before antivenom; give in resuscitation area with adrenaline available; for hypersensitivity stop infusion and give IM adrenaline if severe.
claims.locator: Therapeutic Guidelines (eTG complete), Toxicology and Toxinology guideline: 'Snake bite' at https://app.tg.org.au/viewTopic?etgAccess=true&guidelinePage=Toxicology%20and%20Toxinology&topicfile=what-is-covered-in-toxicology-toxinology&guidelinename=auto&sectionId=c_snake_bite, accessed 2026-09-24 through the owner's subscription, section 'Antivenom adverse reactions'

claims.claim: Serum sickness (4-14 days post antivenom), moderate-severe: prednisolone 25-50 mg (child 0.5 mg/kg up to 25 mg) orally daily for up to 7 days.
claims.locator: Therapeutic Guidelines (eTG complete), Toxicology and Toxinology guideline: 'Snake bite' at https://app.tg.org.au/viewTopic?etgAccess=true&guidelinePage=Toxicology%20and%20Toxinology&topicfile=what-is-covered-in-toxicology-toxinology&guidelinename=auto&sectionId=c_snake_bite, accessed 2026-09-24 through the owner's subscription, section 'Serum sickness'

claims.claim: Pressure bandage with immobilisation for all suspected bites within 4 h, kept on until antivenom started or envenoming excluded; observe at least 12 h with serial bloods (at 1 h after bandage removal, 6 h and 12 h); snake venom detection kit no longer recommended; one vial usually sufficient and persistent coagulopathy is not an indication for more antivenom; FFP for active major bleeding after antivenom.
claims.locator: Therapeutic Guidelines (eTG complete), Toxicology and Toxinology guideline: 'Snake bite' at https://app.tg.org.au/viewTopic?etgAccess=true&guidelinePage=Toxicology%20and%20Toxinology&topicfile=what-is-covered-in-toxicology-toxinology&guidelinename=auto&sectionId=c_snake_bite, accessed 2026-09-24 through the owner's subscription, section 'First aid / Key investigations / Observation'
